recognize_zh: 這是一張腦部軸切 T1 加權 MRI，紅色箭頭指向左側額顳葉/腦島外側一個邊界清楚的高訊號病灶，T1 高訊號符合亞急性出血（methemoglobin），配合 AML 病史提示顱內出血。
features: Axial T1-weighted MRI of the brain at the level of the lateral ventricles
Well-circumscribed ovoid T1-hyperintense lesion in the left lateral frontotemporal/insular region (red arrow)
Faint surrounding hypointense rim suggestive of perilesional edema
Mild local mass effect without midline shift
No other focal lesion evident on this single slice
describe_en: Axial T1-weighted MR image of the brain shows a well-circumscribed ovoid hyperintense lesion in the left lateral frontotemporal/peri-insular region (arrow) with a faint surrounding hypointense rim and mild local mass effect, without midline shift. Intrinsic T1 hyperintensity in this setting is consistent with subacute intraparenchymal hemorrhage (extracellular or intracellular methemoglobin). In a patient with AML, this is suggestive of CNS hemorrhage related to thrombocytopenia and/or coagulopathy (e.g., DIC in APL or hyperleukocytosis); correlation with CT, susceptibility-weighted imaging and coagulation studies is recommended. A single slice limits assessment of enhancement and extent.

ddx.vs: Myeloid sarcoma is usually iso- to hypointense on T1 with homogeneous enhancement, rather than intrinsically T1-hyperintense like blood products.
Infarcts follow a vascular territory with restricted diffusion, and septic emboli are multiple and ring-enhancing, which DWI and contrast sequences would show.
Angioinvasive fungal lesions in neutropenic patients show ring enhancement and are often multiple, requiring contrast imaging and microbiology.
Occurs with very high blast counts and is often multifocal; distinction depends on the white cell count rather than imaging appearance.
